R-201.description: Chromium renders real templates on Lambda with JavaScript disabled, request blocking and browser reuse.

R-202.description: pdf-lib post-processing produces all eight PDF/A levels with ICC, XMP and safety checks.

R-203.description: All five result channels and ping deliver end to end with the documented failure handling.

R-204.description: HTTP callbacks enforce the allowlist plus DNS and link-local/metadata SSRF checks.

R-205.description: CI render regression compares page count, text and appearance for plain and PDF/A PDFs.

R-206.description: A throughput target is confirmed and verified with Power Tuning and a load test.

R-207.description: Opt-in alarms and a runbook cover rollback, DLQ redrive, template removal and recovery.

R-208.description: Plain and PDF/A smoke jobs verify each release and the first real template is live.

R-209.description: Bootstrap, OIDC deploy, branch protection and rollback are verified in the real AWS account.

R-210.description: The bootstrap deploy role gains the EC2 and VPC permissions required for network modes.

R-211.description: Local Chrome preview restricts file requests to the template directory before Lambda reuse.

R-212.description: Terraform supports creating the worker execution role or using a provided same-account role ARN; default create.

R-213.description: The bootstrap deploy role can pass a provided worker role ARN to Lambda.

R-214.description: The generated worker role consumes jobs and publishes to all delivery channels; a provided role must be equivalent.

R-215.description: Terraform creates and outputs a caller role allowed to publish jobs to the SQS queue, or uses a provided ARN.

R-216.description: The caller role only sends jobs; the worker role only publishes results to configured delivery channels.

R-217.description: A provided caller role is added to the queue's allowed senders without modifying its IAM policy.

R-218.description: The generated caller role trusts configured integrator principals or the deployer account root.
